text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The first defence witness in the defamation lawsuit between former Malawi Education Minister Sam Mpasu and a weekly tabloid, The Democrat, told High Court in Blantyre, the commercial city, that she has sued government for $400,000 (Malawi Kwacha 6-million) or breach of contract after Mpasu cancelled a tender she had won.

- A Malawian serial killer and armed robber Sisilande Phiri may have been responsible for gunning down Army Commander, General Manken Chigawa in April 1995 when he attempted to steal his car in central Malawi, police told a coroner's court in Zomba, more than 60km north east of Blantyre.

- The Malawi Law Society has warned the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) government to respect the High Court ruling that declared a parliamentary bill empowering government to wrestle away former President Kamuzu Banda's financial muscle, null and void.
